The trial court found that the distance of the alternative route was, according to the pleader commissioner's report. 1½ miles and there were pits over that way, while the claimed passage was much shorter and straight, and for convenience, and for profitable and better enjoyment of their lands the plaintiffs were entitled to a passage over schedule 1 land. The suit was decreed and the defendants were permanently restrained from obstructing the plaintiff's right of way over the 1st schedule land. 

 4. The lower appellate court held that the plaintiffs could not establish any right of easement of necessity over the disputed land. The plaintiffs' vendor used to come to 2nd schedule land conveniently by a different route and the plaintiffs were claiming their right since the purchase of the land in 1365 B.S After finding that there was an alternative pathway for the plaintiff to go to the 2nd schedule land, and relying on the case of Kali Pada Bose and others Vs. Fani Bhusan Roy and others, 70 Indian Cases, 173, the appellate court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and dismissed the suit.
